doc.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Listening back to 'A Foggy Day' from the jazz fest
summary: They play her jazz fest recording with Red Tyler; she talks about freedom with her accompanists and the importance of space.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I have you on tape here.
I just thought I would play a little bit.
Oy oy oy. © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
Oh that’s from the jazz fest.
Oh it’s fun. Isn’t it fun to do?
I’m guessing okay this was a little like okay what’s going to happen?
How is this going to end up?
I like what the piano player’s doing too.
Yeah. I think that’s Brian Blade on drums.
Brian Blade? I think that’s Brian Blade playing drums.
Thank you. That was fun to do.
I’ll bet. And live, everybody together, no overdubbing.

Not rehearsed no. That’s one of the other things too that happens, that I have been blessed with is having worked with people like that who, whatever you want to do. “What should I do?” “Whatever you want to do, we’re right there.” So I could take freedoms like we did on this little vamp here you know, just take the freedom and the phrasing, stretching things out, putting that space in between, and they’re right there, they’re right there you know. As long as I want to keep doing it, they’re right there. That’s such fun.
And I noticed something, near that ending, and that was when the people you were playing with didn’t feel compelled to fill up all that space with — oh here’s a space I better fill it.
Space is just as important as the written note. The rests are important.
